title: Exclude funded scalar recoding after one to three BIT omissions
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The exact forward and adjoint screens cover 437,897 configurations for single nonbridge omissions and equal-payload pairs and triples. A surviving sender can arbitrarily change by a multiple of the missing scalar direction at its original slot. The test permits arbitrary terminal redecoding and one affordable nested ferry of that same direction. A literal feasibility control reroutes packet 1310, rewrites ten sender equations and preserves both 680-owner operators at higher paid cost.

## Task and overlap

This is a refined follow-up to [#7852](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7852) at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`, on main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. Baseline and prior fixed-equation or terminal-decoder exclusions [#7830](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7830) at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`, [#7978](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7978) at `dd529bbb031cf87b424d43841a88a009773fa24b`, [#7985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7985) at `251e15df3e0c058a843e7cb13f5882179a4e3afc`. This proof keeps old route incidences and order besides the replacement ferry.

## Validation

In a clean Python 3.12 extraction run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` and `python3 -I -B verify.py`. All six shards, actual ferry corruption and owned retirement controls passed locally.

## Open next questions

Allow a new coded payload using receiver side information, a changed existing incidence, or more than one missing direction. A positive word would require complete physical and finite replay.
